detail: Empty, oversized, or ineffective replacement for tests/test_cli.py

eligibility.rationale: The report describes unexpected behavior of the mdformat tool: it updates file timestamps even when the file content is unchanged. This is a correctness/logic bug in the Python tooling (should avoid touching files when no changes are made). The report includes reproduction steps and a clear expected vs actual behavior.

discovery.rationale: The bug is that mdformat updates file timestamps even when files are unchanged. The write logic that replaces files atomically is implemented in src/mdformat/_util.py (atomic_write). Both the public API (src/mdformat/_api.py) and the CLI (src/mdformat/_cli.py) call atomic_write to persist formatted output; thus changing atomic_write to avoid replacing the file when content would be identical will address the bug in all callers. The appropriate regression test belongs in tests/test_cli.py because existing CLI tests already cover formatting and EOL behavior; adding a test there to assert that mtime is unchanged for already-formatted files fits the existing test structure.

evidence.detail: Definition of atomic_write at lines ~109-117. This function currently creates a temp file and always os.replace(tmp_path, path), which updates file mtime.
Call to atomic_write(f, formatted_md, newline) at the end of file(...) function (line ~76). This shows the API uses atomic_write to persist files.
Call to atomic_write(path, formatted_str, newline) in run(...) (lines ~100-120). This shows the CLI uses atomic_write to persist files.
